strata::kernels\n\n======== src/kernels/cuda/quantize_act.cu ========\n// src/kernels/cuda/quantize_act.cu - P2.S2: quantize an activation the way ggml converts src1.\n//\n// WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL.  `ggml_mul_mat` converts the ACTIVATION (src1) to the weight's `vec_dot_type`\n// before the dot product - the rule established over rounds 119-136 and written into `ref/quant.py` as\n// `apply_src1`.  The CPU expert path already honours it (`bench/micro/cpu_s2.cpp` quantizes to int8 and uses\n// `vpdpbusd`), and its P0.T2 parity passes at 1.461e-06.  The GPU kernels added in rounds 166-177 take FP16\n// activations instead.  **Left that way, the two paths would compute different numbers for different experts\n// of the SAME token** - not a tolerance question, an inconsistency inside one forward pass.\n//\n// Q2_0 IS THE CASE THAT MATTERS: the routed experts are all Q2_0, `Q2_0 -> Q8_0`, and that is 31.64 GiB of the\n// 38 GiB pack.  Q8_K (for the K-quants and IQ4_XS) is the other half of the table and is not here yet.\n//\n// THE THREE SUBTLETIES, each of which was paid for once already and is transcribed rather than recalled:\n//\n//   1. `d32 = amax / 127.0f` is computed in FP32, and the QUANTIZED INTEGERS divide by **d32**, not by the\n//      fp16-rounded value that gets stored.  Conflating the two shifts every quant near a rounding boundary -\n//      measured against ggml's own bytes, 18 of 80 blocks differed, and because Q2_0 experts convert to Q8_0\n//      the error landed in all 48 MoE blocks and made the end-to-end KL WORSE.\n//   2. The reference divides in FLOAT64 (`blk.astype(np.float64) / float(np.float32(d32))`) and rounds with\n//      `rint` - half to even.  This kernel therefore divides in double too: an FP32 division followed by\n//      `rintf` differs from the reference wherever the f32 quotient rounds across a .5 boundary.\n//   3. The DEQUANTIZED value is `q * d16`, the fp16 scale, not `q * d32`.  The block stores fp16 and that is\n//      what a reader multiplies by.\n#include \"strata/kernels/quantize_act.hpp\"\n#include \"strata/kernels/f16_bits.hpp\"\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n\nnamespace strata::kernels {\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr int QK8_0 = 32;\n\n// THE fp16 CONVERSION LIVES IN `strata/kernels/f16_bits.hpp`, and this file used to carry its own copy.\n//\n// Round 198 found the private copy wrong in a way no fixture here could see: it tested `if (exp >= 31)` to\n// detect an out-of-range exponent, which conflates an f32 INF/NAN (raw exponent 255) with a FINITE value too\n// large for fp16.  Every finite overflow - 1e30, 65536, 1e45 - came back as a NaN instead of saturating to\n// inf, and this file's fixture is O(1) throughout, so it passed.  A numpy-generated oracle caught it on its\n// first run.  Three copies of a converter whose failure mode is silent wrong bits was two copies too many.\n\n\n__global__ void quantize_q8_0_kernel(const float* __restrict__ x, uint8_t* __restrict__ blocks,\n                                     long long n_blocks) {\n    const long long b = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (b >= n_blocks) return;\n    const float* xb = x + b * QK8_0;\n    uint8_t* out = blocks + b * 34;                 // { fp16 d ; int8 qs[32] }\n\n    float amax = 0.0f;\n    for (int i = 0; i < QK8_0; ++i) amax = fmaxf(amax, fabsf(xb[i]));\n    if (amax == 0.0f) {\n        // ggml leaves the block zeroed: d = 0 and every q = 0.  Writing the fp16 zero explicitly rather than\n        // skipping keeps the block layout deterministic for the byte comparison.\n        const uint16_t zb = f16_from_f32(0.0f);\n        out[0] = (uint8_t) (zb & 0xFF);\n        out[1] = (uint8_t) (zb >> 8);\n        for (int i = 0; i < QK8_0; ++i) out[2 + i] = 0;\n        return;\n    }\n    const float d32 = amax / 127.0f;\n    const uint16_t d16bits = f16_from_f32(d32);\n    out[0] = (uint8_t) (d16bits & 0xFF);\n    out[1] = (uint8_t) (d16bits >> 8);\n\n    // double division, matching the reference exactly (subtlety 2)\n    for (int i = 0; i < QK8_0; ++i) {\n        double q = rint((double) xb[i] / (double) d32);\n        if (q > 127.0) q = 127.0;\n        if (q < -128.0) q = -128.0;\n        out[2 + i] = (uint8_t) (int8_t) q;\n    }\n}\n\n/// **THE HIT PATH'S QUANTIZER, AND IT EXISTS TO REPRODUCE `act_quant_q8_1` EXACTLY (R4.2h, round 331).**\n///\n/// The engine computes every routed expert twice.  MISSES go through `cpu/expert.cpp:138 act_quant_q8_1`\n/// into the VNNI kernel; HITS went through `quantize_q8_0` above.  **Those are not the same quantization**,\n/// and round 330 measured the difference with both real implementations linked\n/// (`bench/micro/act_quant_parity.cu`):\n///\n///     int8 activations differing : 0 of 2560                       <- this rule's ties are measure-zero\n///     chunks whose SCALE differs : 80 of 80, max rel 4.761e-04     <- 2^-11: fp32 vs the block's fp16\n///\n/// The scale is the difference that matters: `ActQ::scale` is `float` and the CPU kernel multiplies by it\n/// (`expert.cpp:92`), while `row_dot_s2_q8` read `f16_at(xb)` out of the `block_q8_0`.  So this variant\n/// writes the SAME 34-byte blocks (the kernel's indexing is unchanged) **and** a parallel fp32 scale array\n/// carrying `d32` unrounded.\n///\n/// It also adopts the CPU's ROUNDING RULE - multiply by the reciprocal, round half AWAY FROM ZERO - rather\n/// than this file's `rint`.  That is deliberate and it is the opposite of the direction the comment above\n/// argues for.  `quantize_q8_0` was tuned to match **ggml's Q8_0 bytes**, which is right for the pack and for\n/// `moe_hit_parity`.  This function's job is different: it must match **this engine's own CPU reference**,\n/// because a hit and a miss for the same expert on the same layer have to produce the same number.  The CPU\n/// path is the reference - C1 passes on it - so the hit path is brought to it, not the reverse.\n__global__ void quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel(const float* __restrict__ x, uint8_t* __restrict__ blocks,\n                                            float* __restrict__ scales, long long n_blocks) {\n    const long long b = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (b >= n_blocks) return;\n    const float* xb = x + b * QK8_0;\n    uint8_t* out = blocks + b * 34;\n\n    float amax = 0.0f;\n    for (int i = 0; i < QK8_0; ++i) amax = fmaxf(amax, fabsf(xb[i]));\n    // VERBATIM from `cpu/expert.cpp:144-145`, including the `amax > 0` guard, so the fp32 value written here\n    // is bit-identical to the `s` the CPU path used.\n    const float s = amax > 0.f ? amax / 127.f : 0.f;\n    const float inv = s > 0.f ? 1.f / s : 0.f;\n    scales[b] = s;\n\n    const uint16_t d16bits = f16_from_f32(s);\n    out[0] = (uint8_t) (d16bits & 0xFF);\n    out[1] = (uint8_t) (d16bits >> 8);\n    for (int i = 0; i < QK8_0; ++i) {\n        // VERBATIM from `cpu/expert.cpp:159-162`: reciprocal multiply, then `t + copysign(0.5, t)` truncated\n        // toward zero, which is `lround`'s rule - round half away from zero.\n        const float t = xb[i] * inv;\n        const float r = t + (t >= 0.f ? 0.5f : -0.5f);\n        int v = (int) r;\n        v = v < -127 ? -127 : (v > 127 ? 127 : v);\n        out[2 + i] = (uint8_t) (int8_t) v;\n    }\n}\n\n__global__ void dequant_q8_0_kernel(const uint8_t* __restrict__ blocks, float* __restrict__ x,\n                                    long long n_blocks) {\n    const long long b = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (b >= n_blocks) return;\n    const uint8_t* blk = blocks + b * 34;\n    const uint16_t dbits = (uint16_t) (blk[0] | (blk[1] << 8));\n    const float d = f32_from_f16(dbits);\n    float* out = x + b * QK8_0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < QK8_0; ++i) out[i] = (float) (int8_t) blk[2 + i] * d;\n}\n\n// ===================== Q8_K =====================\n//\n// `block_q8_K` = { float d ; int8_t qs[256] ; int16_t bsums[16] } = 292 bytes, no padding\n// (`static_assert` in ggml-common.h).  QK_K = 256.\n\nconstexpr int QK_K = 256;\nconstexpr int Q8K_BYTES = 292;\n\n/// ggml's `nearest_int` (ggml-quants.c L621), transcribed rather than replaced.\n///\n/// The magic number is 1.5 * 2^23: adding it forces the mantissa's integer part into the low bits, and the\n/// mask/subtract recover it.  The reason it is transcribed and not written as `rintf` is that the two differ\n/// on exact ties - and that is the whole point of the constant, so a \"cleaner\" rewrite would silently change\n/// which way ties go.\n__device__ __forceinline__ int nearest_int_dev(float fval) {\n    const float val = fval + 12582912.0f;\n    int i;\n    memcpy(&i, &val, 4);\n    return (i & 0x007fffff) - 0x00400000;\n}\n\n__global__ void quantize_q8_K_kernel(const float* __restrict__ x, uint8_t* __restrict__ blocks,\n                                     long long n_blocks) {\n    const long long b = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (b >= n_blocks) return;\n    const float* xb = x + b * QK_K;\n    uint8_t* out = blocks + b * Q8K_BYTES;\n    float* d = (float*) out;\n    int8_t* qs = (int8_t*) (out + 4);\n    int16_t* bsums = (int16_t*) (out + 4 + QK_K);\n\n    // `max` is the SIGNED value at the largest magnitude position, and the comparison is STRICTLY greater,\n    // so a tie keeps the FIRST maximum - which is what `np.argmax` does in the reference transcription too.\n    float max = 0.0f, amax = 0.0f;\n    for (int j = 0; j < QK_K; ++j) {\n        const float ax = fabsf(xb[j]);\n        if (ax > amax) {\n            amax = ax;\n            max = xb[j];\n        }\n    }\n    if (amax == 0.0f) {\n        // ggml writes d = 0 and zeroes qs, then `continue`s - which LEAVES bsums UNWRITTEN.  A zeroed block\n        // and an untouched one are indistinguishable to the dot product, but not to a byte comparison, so\n        // this zeroes bsums as well and the parity test's reference does the same.  Recorded because it is a\n        // deliberate divergence from the letter of the source.\n        *d = 0.0f;\n        for (int j = 0; j < QK_K; ++j) qs[j] = 0;\n        for (int j = 0; j < QK_K / 16; ++j) bsums[j] = 0;\n        return;\n    }\n    const float iscale = -127.0f / max;          // -127, NOT -128; see the header\n    for (int j = 0; j < QK_K; ++j) {\n        // `__fmul_rn`, NOT `iscale * xb[j]`.  ggml computes the product, ROUNDS IT TO F32, and then adds\n        // 12582912.0f inside `nearest_int`.  Written as a plain expression, nvcc CONTRACTS the multiply into\n        // the add as an FMA - which is a more accurate product but not the same one, and it flips the result\n        // wherever the true product sits just off a .5 boundary.  The first version of this kernel differed\n        // from the reference in 1 element of 524,288 for exactly this reason, and `__fmul_rn` pins the\n        // rounding step the source actually performs.\n        const int v = nearest_int_dev(__fmul_rn(iscale, xb[j]));\n        qs[j] = (int8_t) min(127, v);            // MIN only - the source has no lower clamp\n    }\n    for (int j = 0; j < QK_K / 16; ++j) {\n        int sum = 0;\n        for (int ii = 0; ii < 16; ++ii) sum += qs[j * 16 + ii];\n        bsums[j] = (int16_t) sum;\n    }\n    *d = 1.0f / iscale;\n}\n\n__global__ void dequant_q8_K_kernel(const uint8_t* __restrict__ blocks, float* __restrict__ x,\n                                    long long n_blocks) {\n    const long long b = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (b >= n_blocks) return;\n    const uint8_t* blk = blocks + b * Q8K_BYTES;\n    float d;\n    memcpy(&d, blk, 4);\n    const int8_t* qs = (const int8_t*) (blk + 4);\n    float* out = x + b * QK_K;\n    for (int i = 0; i < QK_K; ++i) out[i] = (float) qs[i] * d;\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nvoid quantize_q8_0(const float* x, uint8_t* blocks, int64_t n, void* stream) {\n    if (n <= 0) return;\n    if (n % QK8_0 != 0) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_0: n %lld is not a multiple of %d\\n\", (long long) n, QK8_0);\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    const long long nb = n / QK8_0;\n    const int threads = 128;\n    const unsigned grid = (unsigned) ((nb + threads - 1) / threads);\n    quantize_q8_0_kernel<<<grid, threads, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(x, blocks, nb);\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_0 launch: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (stream == nullptr) cudaDeviceSynchronize();\n}\n\n/// See `quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel`.  Writes the same 34-byte `block_q8_0` layout as `quantize_q8_0`, plus\n/// `scales[n/32]` carrying the fp32 `s` the CPU path used - so a hit can be computed with the CPU's\n/// multiplier instead of the block's fp16 `d`.  `scales` must not be null.\nvoid quantize_q8_0_scaled(const float* x, uint8_t* blocks, float* scales, int64_t n, void* stream) {\n    if (n <= 0) return;\n    if (n % QK8_0 != 0) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_0_scaled: n %lld is not a multiple of %d\\n\", (long long) n, QK8_0);\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (scales == nullptr) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_0_scaled: scales is null\\n\");\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    const long long nb = n / QK8_0;\n    const int threads = 128;\n    const unsigned grid = (unsigned) ((nb + threads - 1) / threads);\n    quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel<<<grid, threads, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(x, blocks, scales, nb);\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_0_scaled launch: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (stream == nullptr) cudaDeviceSynchronize();\n}\n\nvoid dequant_q8_0(const uint8_t* blocks, float* x, int64_t n, void* stream) {\n    if (n <= 0) return;\n    const long long nb = n / QK8_0;\n    const int threads = 128;\n    const unsigned grid = (unsigned) ((nb + threads - 1) / threads);\n    dequant_q8_0_kernel<<<grid, threads, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(blocks, x, nb);\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"dequant_q8_0 launch: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (stream == nullptr) cudaDeviceSynchronize();\n}\n\nvoid quantize_q8_K(const float* x, uint8_t* blocks, int64_t n, void* stream) {\n    if (n <= 0) return;\n    if (n % QK_K != 0) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_K: n %lld is not a multiple of %d\\n\", (long long) n, QK_K);\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    const long long nb = n / QK_K;\n    const int threads = 64;                       // one block per thread, and a block is 256 elements\n    const unsigned grid = (unsigned) ((nb + threads - 1) / threads);\n    quantize_q8_K_kernel<<<grid, threads, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(x, blocks, nb);\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"quantize_q8_K launch: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (stream == nullptr) cudaDeviceSynchronize();\n}\n\nvoid dequant_q8_K(const uint8_t* blocks, float* x, int64_t n, void* stream) {\n    if (n <= 0) return;\n    const long long nb = n / QK_K;\n    const int threads = 64;\n    const unsigned grid = (unsigned) ((nb + threads - 1) / threads);\n    dequant_q8_K_kernel<<<grid, threads, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(blocks, x, nb);\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"dequant_q8_K launch: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (stream == nullptr) cudaDeviceSynchronize();\n}\n\n}  // namespace strata::kernels\n\n======== src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu ========\n// src/kernels/cuda/qsa_select.cu - see include/strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp.\n#include \"strata/kernels/qsa_select.hpp\"\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <cfloat>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n\nnamespace strata::kernels {\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr int IDX_DIM = 128, IDX_HEADS = 4, R = 4;\nconstexpr int SCORE_WARPS = 8;\nconstexpr int TOPK_T = 256;\n\n__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t order_key(float s) {\n    const float v = s + 0.0f;\n    if (!(v == v)) return 0u;\n    const uint32_t b = __float_as_uint(v);\n    return (b & 0x80000000u) ? ~b : (b | 0x80000000u);\n}\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(SCORE_WARPS * 32) block_scores_kernel(const float* __restrict__ pooled,\n                                                                        const float* __restrict__ dead,\n                                                                        const float* __restrict__ q_idx,\n                                                                        const int32_t* __restrict__ steps,\n                                                                        int64_t max_blocks, float* __restrict__ out) {\n    const int64_t qi = blockIdx.y;\n    const int32_t* st = steps + qi * kStepCount;\n    const int64_t n_kv = st[kStepNKv], n_bid = st[kStepNBid];\n    const int64_t b = (int64_t) blockIdx.x * SCORE_WARPS + (threadIdx.x >> 5);\n    if (b > n_bid || b >= max_blocks) return;\n    const int lane = threadIdx.x & 31;\n    const float* key = (b == n_bid) ? dead : pooled + b * IDX_DIM;\n    const float4 k4 = *reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(key + lane * 4);\n    const float* q = q_idx + qi * IDX_HEADS * IDX_DIM + lane * 4;\n    float score = 0.0f;\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int h = 0; h < IDX_HEADS; ++h) {\n        const float4 q4 = *reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(q + h * IDX_DIM);\n        float d = k4.x * q4.x + k4.y * q4.y + k4.z * q4.z + k4.w * q4.w;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) d += __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, d, o);\n        score += d > 0.0f ? d : 0.0f;\n    }\n    if (lane == 0) {\n        if (b == n_bid && n_kv % R != 0) score += 1e9f;\n        out[qi * max_blocks + b] = score;\n    }\n}\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TOPK_T) block_topk_kernel(const float* __restrict__ scores,\n                                                            const int32_t* __restrict__ steps, int64_t max_blocks,\n                                                            int64_t cap, int32_t* __restrict__ ids) {\n    __shared__ int hist[256];\n    __shared__ int s_a[TOPK_T], s_b[TOPK_T];\n    __shared__ int s_digit, s_above;\n    const int64_t qi = blockIdx.x;\n    const int32_t* st = steps + qi * kStepCount;\n    const int64_t n_kv = st[kStepNKv], n_bid = st[kStepNBid], width = st[kStepWidth];\n    int32_t* out = ids + qi * cap;\n    const int t = threadIdx.x;\n    if (n_kv <= width) {                               // everything is selected: the identity, ascending\n        for (int64_t j = t; j < n_kv; j += TOPK_T) out[j] = (int32_t) j;\n        return;\n    }\n    const float* sc = scores + qi * max_blocks;\n    const int64_t nb = n_bid + 1;                      // blocks 0..n_bid, the last possibly empty\n    const int64_t per = (nb + TOPK_T - 1) / TOPK_T;\n    const int64_t b0 = (int64_t) t * per, b1 = (b0 + per < nb) ? b0 + per : nb;\n    auto weight = [&](int64_t b) -> int { return b < n_bid ? R : (int) (n_kv - n_bid * R); };\n    // ---- radix select: the largest key thr with (cells with key >= thr) >= width, 8 bits at a time\n    uint32_t prefix = 0;\n    int above = 0;                                     // cells strictly above the digits fixed so far\n    for (int shift = 24; shift >= 0; shift -= 8) {\n        for (int i = t; i < 256; i += TOPK_T) hist[i] = 0;\n        __syncthreads();\n        const uint32_t hi_mask = shift == 24 ? 0u : (0xffffffffu << (shift + 8));\n        for (int64_t b = b0; b < b1; ++b) {\n            const int w = weight(b);\n            if (w == 0) continue;\n            const uint32_t k = order_key(sc[b]);\n            if ((k & hi_mask) == (prefix & hi_mask)) atomicAdd(&hist[(k >> shift) & 255], w);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (t == 0) {\n            int cum = above, d = 255;\n            for (; d > 0; --d) {\n                if (cum + hist[d] >= width) break;\n                cum += hist[d];\n            }\n            s_digit = d;\n            s_above = cum;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n        prefix |= (uint32_t) s_digit << shift;\n        above = s_above;\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n    const uint32_t thr = prefix;\n    const int64_t eq_budget = width - above;          // cells equal to thr that fit, lowest index first\n    // ---- per-thread counts of cells above and at the threshold, then their exclusive prefixes\n    int gt = 0, eq = 0;\n    for (int64_t b = b0; b < b1; ++b) {\n        const int w = weight(b);\n        if (w == 0) continue;\n        const uint32_t k = order_key(sc[b]);\n        if (k > thr) gt += w;\n        else if (k == thr) eq += w;\n    }\n    s_a[t] = gt;\n    s_b[t] = eq;\n    __syncthreads();\n    if (t == 0) {\n        int ag = 0, ae = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < TOPK_T; ++i) {\n            const int g = s_a[i], e = s_b[i];\n            s_a[i] = ag; s_b[i] = ae;\n            ag += g; ae += e;\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n    const int64_t eq_before = s_b[t];\n    int64_t my_eq = eq_budget - eq_before;\n    if (my_eq < 0) my_eq = 0;\n    if (my_eq > eq) my_eq = eq;\n    const int sel = gt + (int) my_eq;\n    __syncthreads();\n    s_a[t] = sel;\n    __syncthreads();\n    if (t == 0) {\n        int a = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < TOPK_T; ++i) { const int c = s_a[i]; s_a[i] = a; a += c; }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n    int64_t wpos = s_a[t];\n    int64_t eq_left = my_eq;\n    for (int64_t b = b0; b < b1; ++b) {\n        const int w = weight(b);\n        if (w == 0) continue;\n        const uint32_t k = order_key(sc[b]);\n        if (k > thr) {\n            for (int c = 0; c < w; ++c) out[wpos++] = (int32_t) (b * R + c);\n        } else if (k == thr) {\n            for (int c = 0; c < w && eq_left > 0; ++c, --eq_left) out[wpos++] = (int32_t) (b * R + c);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nvoid qsa_block_scores(const float* pooled, const float* dead, const float* q_idx, const int32_t* steps, int64_t nq,\n                      int64_t max_blocks, const QsaShapes& s, float* scores, void* stream) {\n    if (nq <= 0) return;\n    if (s.idx_dim != IDX_DIM || s.idx_n_head != IDX_HEADS || s.idx_block != R || nq > 65535) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"qsa_block_scores: unsupported indexer geometry\\n\");\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    const dim3 grid((unsigned) ((max_blocks + SCORE_WARPS - 1) / SCORE_WARPS), (unsigned) nq);\n    block_scores_kernel<<<grid, SCORE_WARPS * 32, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(pooled, dead, q_idx, steps, max_blocks,\n cudaGetErrorString(e)); std::exit(1); }\n}\n\nvoid qsa_block_topk(const float* scores, const int32_t* steps, int64_t nq, int64_t max_blocks, int64_t cap,\n                    const QsaShapes& s, int32_t* ids, void* stream) {\n    if (nq <= 0) return;\n    if (s.idx_block != R || cap < qsa_selection_width(kTopkMaxCells, s)) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"qsa_block_topk: unsupported geometry or cap\\n\");\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    block_topk_kernel<<<(unsigned) nq, TOPK_T, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(scores, steps, max_blocks, cap, ids);\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) { std::fprintf(stderr, \"qsa_block_topk: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e)); std::exit(1); }\n}\n\n}  // namespace strata::kernels\n\n======== src/kernels/cuda/kv_q8.cu ========\n// src/kernels/cuda/kv_q8.cu - see include/strata/kernels/kv_q8.hpp.\n#include \"strata/kernels/kv_q8.hpp\"\n#include \"strata/kernels/f16_bits.hpp\"\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n\nnamespace strata::kernels {\nnamespace {\n\nvoid check(const char* what) {\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"kv_q8: %s: %s\\n\", what, cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid validate(const QsaShapes& s, const char* what) {\n    if (s.head_dim % KV_Q8_GROUP != 0 || s.n_head_kv <= 0 || s.page_size <= 0) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"kv_q8: %s: head_dim %lld must be a multiple of %d\\n\", what, (long long) s.head_dim,\n                     KV_Q8_GROUP);\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n}\n\n// One block = one 64-value group of one KV head of K (blockIdx.z = 0) or V (1); 64 threads, one value each.\n__global__ void kv_append_q8_kernel(int8_t* __restrict__ k_q, int8_t* __restrict__ v_q,\n                                    uint16_t* __restrict__ k_scale, uint16_t* __restrict__ v_scale,\n                                    const int32_t* __restrict__ table, const int32_t* __restrict__ step,\n                                    const float* __restrict__ kcur, const float* __restrict__ vcur, int kv_heads,\n                                    int head_dim, int page_size) {\n    const long long pos = (long long) __ldg(step + kStepPos);\n    const int h = blockIdx.x, g = blockIdx.y, t = threadIdx.x;\n    const bool is_v = blockIdx.z == 1;\n    const int groups = head_dim / KV_Q8_GROUP;\n    const float x = (is_v ? vcur : kcur)[h * head_dim + g * KV_Q8_GROUP + t];\n    // max |x| over the 64 values: two warps, then combine through shared memory in a fixed order\n    float a = fabsf(x);\n    for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) a = fmaxf(a, __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, a, o));\n    __shared__ float warp_max[2];\n    if ((t & 31) == 0) warp_max[t >> 5] = a;\n    __syncthreads();\n    const float amax = fmaxf(warp_max[0], warp_max[1]);\n    const uint16_t sbits = f16_from_f32(amax / 127.0f);\n    const float sf = f32_from_f16(sbits);                          // quantize against the STORED scale\n    int q = 0;\n    if (sf > 0.0f) {\n        q = __float2int_rn(x / sf);\n        q = q < -127 ? -127 : (q > 127 ? 127 : q);\n    }\n    const long long page = (long long) table[pos / page_size];\n    const long long row = (page * kv_heads + h) * page_size + (pos % page_size);\n    (is_v ? v_q : k_q)[row * head_dim + g * KV_Q8_GROUP + t] = (int8_t) q;\n    if (t == 0) (is_v ? v_scale : k_scale)[row * groups + g] = sbits;\n}\n\n// One thread = 4 consecutive values of one cell and head (as the FP16 gather does with uint2).\n__global__ void kv_gather_q8_kernel(const int8_t* __restrict__ k_q, const int8_t* __restrict__ v_q,\n                                    const uint16_t* __restrict__ k_scale, const uint16_t* __restrict__ v_scale,\n                                    const int32_t* __restrict__ table, const int32_t* __restrict__ ids,\n                                    const int32_t* __restrict__ step, int kv_heads, int head_dim, int page_size,\n                                    uint16_t* __restrict__ k_scratch, uint16_t* __restrict__ v_scratch) {\n    const long long n_ids = (long long) __ldg(step + kStepWidth);\n    const int per = head_dim / 4;\n    const long long total = n_ids * kv_heads * per;\n    const long long i = blockIdx.x * (long long) blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (i >= total) return;\n    const long long id = i / (kv_heads * (long long) per);\n    const int rem = (int) (i % (kv_heads * (long long) per));\n    const int h = rem / per, q4 = rem - h * per;\n    const int cell = ids[id];\n    const long long page = (long long) table[cell / page_size];\n    const long long row = (page * kv_heads + h) * page_size + (cell % page_size);\n    const int d = q4 * 4;\n    const int groups = head_dim / KV_Q8_GROUP;\n    const float ks = f32_from_f16(k_scale[row * groups + d / KV_Q8_GROUP]);\n    const float vs = f32_from_f16(v_scale[row * groups + d / KV_Q8_GROUP]);\n    const char4 kc = reinterpret_cast<const char4*>(k_q + row * head_dim)[q4];\n    const char4 vc = reinterpret_cast<const char4*>(v_q + row * head_dim)[q4];\n    ushort4 ko, vo;\n    ko.x = f16_from_f32((float) kc.x * ks); ko.y = f16_from_f32((float) kc.y * ks);\n    ko.z = f16_from_f32((float) kc.z * ks); ko.w = f16_from_f32((float) kc.w * ks);\n    vo.x = f16_from_f32((float) vc.x * vs); vo.y = f16_from_f32((float) vc.y * vs);\n    vo.z = f16_from_f32((float) vc.z * vs); vo.w = f16_from_f32((float) vc.w * vs);\n    const long long dst = (id * kv_heads + h) * (long long) per + q4;\n    reinterpret_cast<ushort4*>(k_scratch)[dst] = ko;\n    reinterpret_cast<ushort4*>(v_scratch)[dst] = vo;\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nvoid kv_append_q8_step(int8_t* k_q, int8_t* v_q, uint16_t* k_scale, uint16_t* v_scale, const int32_t* page_table,\n                       const int32_t* step, const float* kcur, const float* vcur, const QsaShapes& s, void* stream) {\n    k_q, v_q, k_scale, v_scale, page_table, step, kcur, vcur, (int) s.n_head_kv, (int) s.head_dim,\n        (int) s.page_size);\n    check(\"kv_append_q8 launch\");\n}\n\nvoid kv_gather_q8_step(const int8_t* k_q, const int8_t* v_q, const uint16_t* k_scale, const uint16_t* v_scale,\n                       const int32_t* page_table, const int32_t* ids, const int32_t* step, int64_t max_ids,\n                       const QsaShapes& s, uint16_t* k_scratch, uint16_t* v_scratch, void* stream) {\n    validate(s, \"kv_gather_q8\");\n    if (max_ids <= 0) return;\n    const long long total = max_ids * s.n_head_kv * (s.head_dim / 4);\n    const unsigned blocks = (unsigned) ((total + 255) / 256);\n    kv_gather_q8_kernel<<<blocks, 256, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(\n        k_q, v_q, k_scale, v_scale, page_table, ids, step, (int) s.n_head_kv, (int) s.head_dim, (int) s.page_size,\n        k_scratch, v_scratch);\n    check(\"kv_gather_q8 launch\");\n}\n\n}  // namespace strata::kernels\n\n======== src/kernels/cuda/rope.cu ========\n// src/kernels/cuda/rope.cu - P2.S2: NEOX partial RoPE.\n//\n// Semantics from `ref/qsa.py` (`rope_freqs` + `rope_neox`), which `bench/micro/rope_xcheck` validates against\n// the oracle:\n//\n//     inv[i] = theta ** (-2i / n_rot)          i in [0, n_rot/2)\n//     ang    = pos * inv\n//     cos, sin = cos(ang), sin(ang)\n//     out[:half]     = a*cos - b*sin            a = x[:half], b = x[half:n_rot]\n//     out[half:n_rot] = a*sin + b*cos\n//\n// THE PAIRING IS NEOX - (i, i + n_rot/2), NOT the adjacent pair (2i, 2i+1).  `ggml.h` writes NEOX\n// n_dims=8 as [ccccssss]; the adjacent-pair (\"NORMAL\") ordering is the other common convention and choosing\n// wrongly rotates the wrong dimensions together, which produces correctly-shaped output with scrambled\n// content.  It is also PARTIAL: only the first n_rot of head_dim are touched, here 64 of 256.\n//\n// WHY THE TABLE IS BUILT ON THE HOST.  The reference computes the frequencies in FLOAT64 (`theta ** (...)`\n// on a float64 arange, cos/sin in float64).  Reproducing that on device means double-precision pow and cos,\n// which are slow on a consumer GPU and - more to the point - not guaranteed to agree with the host's libm.\n// Building the table once on the host and passing it in makes the TABLE exactly the reference's values and\n// leaves the kernel a pure rotation, so each half can be checked tightly instead of both halves sharing one\n// loose tolerance.  The engine wants a cached table anyway: it is per (n_rot, theta, position), not per token.\n#include \"strata/kernels/rope.hpp\"\n#include \"strata/kernels/mrope.hpp\"\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n\nnamespace strata::kernels {\n\nvoid build_rope_table(int n_rot, double theta, int max_pos, float* cos_tab, float* sin_tab) {\n    const int half = n_rot / 2;\n    for (int p = 0; p < max_pos; ++p) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < half; ++i) {\n            // float64 throughout, in the reference's order: inv, then ang, then cos/sin\n            const double inv = std::pow(theta, -2.0 * (double) i / (double) n_rot);\n            const double ang = (double) p * inv;\n            cos_tab[(size_t) p * half + i] = (float) std::cos(ang);\n            sin_tab[(size_t) p * half + i] = (float) std::sin(ang);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nnamespace {\n\n// ONE THREAD PER ROW, not per (row, pair).  The first version had one thread per pair and did the tail copy\n// with \threadIdx.x strided loops - so up to 32 threads wrote into the SAME row, with no barrier between the\n// copy and the rotation, and a thread's copy of orow[i] could land AFTER another thread had rotated it.  A\n// race that silently writes the unrotated value is worse than a wrong answer: it is intermittent.\n//\n// A row is head_dim floats (256 here) and there are batch x heads of them, so one thread per row is a\n// handful of threads for a token and removes the ordering question entirely rather than synchronising it.\n__global__ void rope_neox_kernel(const float* __restrict__ x, float* __restrict__ out, long long rows,\n                                 int head_dim, int n_rot, const float* __restrict__ cos_tab,\n                                 const float* __restrict__ sin_tab, const int* __restrict__ pos,\n                                 const int32_t* __restrict__ mtab) {\n    const long long r = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (r >= rows) return;\n    const int half = n_rot / 2;\n    const float* xr = x + r * head_dim;\n    float* orow = out + r * head_dim;\n\n    for (int d = n_rot; d < head_dim; ++d) orow[d] = xr[d];      // the PARTIAL rotation's untouched tail\n    for (int i = 0; i < half; ++i) {\n        const size_t toff = (size_t) mrope_pos(mtab, pos[r], i) * half;   // the image path's per-pair position\n        // THE PAIRING AND THE SIGNS COME FROM `rope_neox_pair`, shared with the indexer's pooling kernel.\n        rope_neox_pair(xr[i], xr[half + i], cos_tab[toff + i], sin_tab[toff + i], orow[i], orow[half + i]);\n    }\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\nvoid rope_neox_apply(const float* x, float* out, int64_t rows, int head_dim, int n_rot, const float* cos_tab,\n                     const float* sin_tab, const int* pos, void* stream) {\n    if (rows <= 0 || n_rot <= 0) return;\n    if (n_rot % 2 != 0 || n_rot > head_dim) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"rope_neox_apply: n_rot %d must be even and <= head_dim %d\\n\", n_rot, head_dim);\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    const int threads = 128;\n    const unsigned grid = (unsigned) ((rows + threads - 1) / threads);\n    rope_neox_kernel<<<grid, threads, 0, (cudaStream_t) stream>>>(x, out, rows, head_dim, n_rot, cos_tab,\n                                                                 sin_tab, pos, mrope_table());\n    const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();\n    if (e != cudaSuccess) {\n        std::fprintf(stderr, \"rope_neox_apply launch: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(e));\n        std::exit(1);\n    }\n    if (stream == nullptr) cudaDeviceSynchronize();\n}\n\n}  // namespace strata::kernels\n\n======== src/kernels/cuda/native_moe.cu ========\n// Arithmetic adapted from the MIT-licensed pinned ggml CUDA\n// moe-weighted-reduction.cu at 3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d.\n// MIT License\n// Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors\n//\n// Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy\n// of this software and associated documentation files (the \"Software\"), to deal\n// in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights\n// to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell\n// copies of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is\n// furnished to do so, subject to the following conditions:\n//\n// The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all\n// copies or substantial portions of the Software.\n//\n// THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED \"AS IS\", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR\n// IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,\n// FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. <cstdint>\n#include <limits>\n#include <stdexcept>\n\nnamespace strata::kernels {\nnamespace {\nstd::atomic<bool> enabled{false};\n__global__ void combine(const float* __restrict__ parts, const float* __restrict__ weights,\n                        const float* __restrict__ shared, float* __restrict__ output,\n                        int64_t n_embd, int k) {\n    const int64_t col = int64_t(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (col >= n_embd) return;\n    float sum = parts[col] * weights[0];\n    for (int expert = 1; expert < k; ++expert) {\n        sum += parts[int64_t(expert) * n_embd + col] * weights[expert];\n    }\n    if (shared) sum += shared[col];\n    output[col] = sum;\n}\nbool valid_span(const void* p, size_t bytes) {\n    const auto address = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(p);\n    return p && address % alignof(float) == 0 && bytes <= UINTPTR_MAX - address;\n}\nbool overlap(const void* a, size_t an, const void* b, size_t bn) {\n    const ## MODULE: iq_format_kernels (importance-quantized format dot products, dequantizers, and grouped experts)

**Source scope:** 720 lines. Provides vec_dot functions for IQ formats (IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ1_M, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS) plus Q2_0 and Q3_K against Q8_1 activations, using llama.cpp's codebook grids. Also contains dequantizers for all formats, a templated MMVQ kernel, a Q8_1 quantizer, embedding-row dequantization, and grouped native expert kernels dispatched by format type.

### SUBMODULE: iq_vec_dot_family (IQ format dot products against Q8_1)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Each IQ format stores weights as indices into precomputed codebook grids. The dot products share a pattern:

1. **Grid lookup:** A codebook index (from `qs`) maps to an `(x, y)` pair of int8×4 vectors from a grid table (e.g., `iq2xxs_grid`, `iq3xxs_grid`, `iq3s_grid`).

2. **Sign application:** Sign bits are unpacked from the block's sign field via `unpack_ksigns`, then applied using `__vcmpne4` + `__vsub4` (XOR-subtract pattern):
$$
\text{signed} = (v \oplus \text{signs}) - \text{signs}
$$

3. **DP4A accumulation:** Each signed grid vector is dotted against the Q8_1 activation via `__dp4a`.

4. **Scale application:** Format-specific scale extraction, then:
$$
\text{result} = d_w \cdot d_8 \cdot f(\text{sumi}, \text{scales})
$$

**IQ2_XXS** ($QK = 256$, $QI = 8$):
$$
\text{sumi} = \sum_{k} \text{dp4a}(\text{grid}^{(k)}_{\text{signed}}, u_k)
$$
$$
\text{ls} = (\text{aux32} \gg 27) \;|\; 1, \quad \text{result} = d \cdot d_8 \cdot \frac{\text{sumi} \cdot \text{ls}}{8}
$$

**IQ2_XS** ($QK = 256$, $QI = 8$): 4-bit per-pair scales, split accumulation:
$$
\text{result} = d \cdot d_8 \cdot \frac{\text{sumi}_0 \cdot \text{ls}_0 + \text{sumi}_1 \cdot \text{ls}_1 + \lfloor(\text{sumi}_0 + \text{sumi}_1)/2\rfloor}{4}
$$

**IQ3_XXS** ($QK = 256$, $QI = 8$): 4-bit scale from aux32:
$$
\text{ls} = \text{aux32} \gg 28, \quad \text{result} = d \cdot d_8 \cdot \frac{\text{ls} \cdot \text{sumi} + \lfloor\text{sumi}/2\rfloor}{2}
$$

**IQ3_S** ($QK = 256$, $QI = 8$): Scale with odd multiplier:
$$
\text{sumi} \mathrel{\times}= 1 + 2 \cdot ((\text{scales}[\lfloor\text{iqs}/4\rfloor] \gg ((\text{iqs} \ll 1) \;\&\; 4)) \;\&\; \texttt{0x0F})
$$

**IQ1_M** ($QK = 256$, $QI = 8$): Grid from `iq1s_grid_gpu`, delta correction, packed 3-bit scales:
$$
\text{result} = d \cdot ((\text{sumi}_0 + \text{sumf}_0) \cdot \text{sc}_0 + (\text{sumi}_1 + \text{sumf}_1) \cdot \text{sc}_1)
$$
where $\text{sc}_i = 2 \cdot ((\text{tmp} \gg 3i) \;\&\; 7) + 1$.

**IQ4_NL** ($QK = 32$, $QI = 2$): Nonlinear codebook via `get_int_from_table_16` (same as `iq4_table_lookup` in native_mmvq).

```cuda
template<int TY> struct adjFmt;
template<> struct adjFmt<16> {
    static constexpr int qk = 256, ipb = 8, step = 2;
    __device__ static float dot(const void* vname, const typenameQ8Block* yname, int kbxname, int iqsname) {
        return adj_vec_dot_iq2_xxs(vname, yname, kbxname, iqsname);
    }
};
// ... one specialization per format type ...

template<int TY>
__device__ __forceinline__ float adj_row_dot(
    const uint8_t* rowname, const typenameQ8Block* xname, int nbname, int lane) {
    using F = adjFmt<TY>;
    float s = 0.0f;
    for (int k = lane; k < nbname * F::ipb; k += 32) {
        const int kbxname = k / F::ipb, iqsname = F::step * (k % F::ipb);
        s += F::dot(rowname, xname + kbxname * (F::qk / 32), kbxname, iqsname);
    }
    return warp_sum(s);
}
```

### SUBMODULE: iq_mmvq_generic (templated MMVQ kernel for IQ formats)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

$$
y[c \cdot N_{out} + r] = \sum_{k} \text{row\_dot}\langle TY \rangle(W[r], X[c \cdot (N_{in}/32)], N_{in}/QK, \text{lane})
$$

Grid: $\lceil N_{out}/4 \rceil$ blocks, each with $4 \times 32$ threads (4 warps of 32 lanes). Supports multi-column ($\text{ncols}$) for batched MMVQ.

**Key difference from native_mmvq:** This kernel uses the llama.cpp block structs (from `ggml-common.h`) while native_mmvq defines its own pinned structs. The two coexist for different format sets.

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cuda
template<int TY>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(128) adj_mmvq_kernel(
    const uint8_t* __restrict__ wname, size_t row_bytesname,
    const typenameQ8Block* __restrict__ xname,
    float* __restrict__ yname, int n_inname, int n_outname, int ncolsname) {
    const int rowname = blockIdx.x * 4 + threadIdx.y;
    if (rowname >= n_outname) return;
    const int lane = threadIdx.x;
    const int nbname = n_inname / adjFmt<TY>::qk;
    const uint8_t* wrname = wname + (size_t) rowname * row_bytesname;
    for (int c = 0; c < ncolsname; ++c) {
        const float s = adj_row_dot<TY>(wrname, xname + (size_t) c * (n_inname / 32), nbname, lane);
        if (lane == 0) yname[(size_t) c * n_outname + rowname] = s;
    }
}
```

### SUBMODULE: iq_dequantizers (per-format dequantization to float or half)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Each dequantizer converts one "superblock" ($QK\_K = 256$ elements, or $QK = 32/64$ for smaller formats) from packed quantized form to float/half. Thread $t$ writes 8 values at a specific position within the superblock.

**Common pattern for grid-based formats (IQ2, IQ3):**

$$
y[j] = d \cdot \text{grid}[j] \cdot \text{sign}[j], \quad \text{sign}[j] \in \{-1, +1\}
$$

where $d$ includes the block scale and subgroup scale factors.

**Q2_0 dequant:** Thread $t$ handles block $t/8$, 8 values each:
$$
y[i] = d \cdot (\text{code}[i] - 1), \quad \text{code}[i] \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}
$$

**IQ4_XS dequant:** Uses the nonlinear `kvalues_iq4nl` table:
$$
y[j] = d \cdot T[q_4[j] \;\&\; \texttt{0xf}], \quad y[j+16] = d \cdot T[q_4[j] \gg 4]
$$

**Q3_K dequant:** 64 threads folded onto 32 (each thread handles 2 passes):
$$
y[l] = d \cdot \text{scale} \cdot ((\text{qs}[l] \gg \text{shift}) \;\&\; 3 - (\text{hmask}[l] \;\&\; m \;?\; 0 : 4))
$$

### SUBMODULE: iq_native_grouped_expert (grouped native expert dispatch for IQ formats)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Templated expert gate/up and down projections using the `row_dot<TY>` function.

**Gate/Up kernel:** Grid $(2 \cdot N_{ff} / 8, N_{\text{groups}})$, 256 threads (8 warps). Each warp takes one row of one group's blob, iterates over all entries $[e_0, e_1)$ in that group:

$$
\text{out}_{e,r} = \text{row\_dot}\langle TG \rangle(W_r, X_{\text{tok}[e]})
$$

Gate and up are separate output buffers (not interleaved like `s2_expert_grouped`).

**SwiGLU:**
$$
h[i] = \frac{g[i]}{1 + e^{-g[i]}} \cdot u[i]
$$

**Down kernel:** Same structure, $N_{embd}$ output rows:
$$
\text{out}[\text{dst}[e] \cdot N_{embd} + r] = \text{row\_dot}\langle TD \rangle(W_r^D, h_{Q8,e})
$$

**Layout struct `NativeExpertLayout`:**
- `gu_row`: bytes per gate/up row
- `up_off = n_ff * gu_row`
- `down_off = 2 * up_off`
- `bytes = down_off + n_embd * d_row`

```cuda
template<int TG>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256) adj_native_gu_kernel(
    const unsigned long long* __restrict__ grp_ptrname,
    const int32_t* __restrict__ grp_startname,
    const int32_t* __restrict__ n_groupsname,
    const int32_t* __restrict__ ent_tokname,
    const typenameQ8Block* __restrict__ xqname,
    typenameExpertLayout Lname,
    float* __restrict__ gatename, float* __restrict__ upname) {
    const int gname = blockIdx.y;
    if (gname >= *n_groupsname) return;
    const int warp = threadIdx.x >> 5, lane = threadIdx.x & 31;
    const int rowname = blockIdx.x * GU_ROWS + warp;
    if (rowname >= 2 * Lname.n_ff) return;
    const bool is_up = rowname >= Lname.n_ff;
    const int r = is_up ? rowname - (int) Lname.n_ff : rowname;
    const uint8_t* blob = (const uint8_t*) grp_ptrname[gname];
    const uint8_t* wrname = blob + (is_up ? Lname.up_off : 0) + (size_t) r * Lname.gu_row;
    const int e0 = grp_startname[gname], e1 = grp_startname[gname + 1];
    for (int e = e0; e < e1; ++e) {
        const float s = adj_row_dot<TG>(wrname, xqname + (size_t) ent_tokname[e] * xbname, nbname, lane);
        if (lane == 0) (is_up ? upname : gatename)[(size_t) e * Lname.n_ff + r] = s;
    }
}
```

## MODULE: activation_quantizer (Q8_0, Q8_0_scaled, Q8_K quantize/dequant)

**Source scope:** 313 lines. CUDA kernels for activation quantization: Q8_0 (for GGML mat-vec), Q8_0_scaled (matching CPU expert path's fp32 scale contract), Q8_K (for K-quants with bsums), plus their dequantizers. Documents three critical numerical subtleties.

---

### SUBMODULE: quantize_q8_0 (standard Q8_0 activation quantization)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

For each 32-element block $b$:

$$
a_{\max} = \max_i |x_i|, \quad d_{32} = \frac{a_{\max}}{127}
$$

**Subtlety 1:** The integers are quantized against $d_{32}$ (fp32), NOT the fp16-rounded scale:
$$
q_i = \text{rint}\!\left(\frac{x_i}{d_{32}}\right), \quad \text{in double precision}
$$

**Subtlety 2:** Division in float64 + `rint` (half-to-even) matches the reference.

**Subtlety 3:** Dequantized value uses fp16 scale: $\hat{x}_i = q_i \cdot d_{16}$.

Output: 34-byte block `{fp16 d, int8 qs[32]}`.

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cuda
__global__ void adj_quantize_q8_0_kernel(const float* __restrict__ xname,
                                          uint8_t* __restrict__ blocksname,
                                          long long n_blocksname) {
    const long long bname = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (bname >= n_blocksname) return;
    const float* xb = xname + bname * QK8_0;
    uint8_t* outname = blocksname + bname * 34;
    float amaxname = 0.0f;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < QK8_0; ++idx) amaxname = fmaxf(amaxname, fabsf(xb[idx]));
    if (amaxname == 0.0f) { /* zero block */ return; }
    const float d32name = amaxname / 127.0f;
    const uint16_t d16name = f16_from_f32(d32name);
    outname[0] = (uint8_t) (d16name & 0xFF);
    outname[1] = (uint8_t) (d16name >> 8);
    for (int idx = 0; idx < QK8_0; ++idx) {
        double qname = rint((double) xb[idx] / (double) d32name);
        if (qname > 127.0) qname = 127.0;
        if (qname < -128.0) qname = -128.0;
        outname[2 + idx] = (uint8_t) (int8_t) qname;
    }
}
```

### SUBMODULE: quantize_q8_0_scaled (CPU-parity activation quantization)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Purpose:** Match the CPU expert path's quantization contract exactly (R4.2h), so cache hits and misses produce identical results.

$$
s = \begin{cases} a_{\max} / 127 & \text{if } a_{\max} > 0 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \quad
\text{inv} = \begin{cases} 1/s & \text{if } s > 0 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
$$

**Rounding rule (differs from `quantize_q8_0`):** Reciprocal multiply, round half away from zero:
$$
t = x_i \cdot \text{inv}, \quad r = t + \text{copysign}(0.5, t), \quad q_i = \text{trunc}(r)
$$

**Output:** Same 34-byte blocks + parallel `float scales[n/32]` carrying unrounded $s$.

**Critical:** The 80-of-80 chunks scale disagreement ($4.761 \times 10^{-4}$ relative) between fp32 $s$ and fp16 $d$ is what this kernel exists to resolve.

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean
-- proof_needed: copysign(0.5, t) + t rounds away from zero for half-integers
```

```cuda
__global__ void adj_quantize_q8_0_scaled_kernel(
    const float* __restrict__ xname, uint8_t* __restrict__ blocksname,
    float* __restrict__ scalesname, long long n_blocksname) {
    const long long bname = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (bname >= n_blocksname) return;
    const float* xb = xname + bname * QK8_0;
    uint8_t* outname = blocksname + bname * 34;
    float amaxname = 0.0f;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < QK8_0; ++idx) amaxname = fmaxf(amaxname, fabsf(xb[idx]));
    const float sname = amaxname > 0.f ? amaxname / 127.f : 0.f;
    const float invname = sname > 0.f ? 1.f / sname : 0.f;
    scalesname[bname] = sname;
    // ... write d16, then round-half-away-from-zero quantize ...
}
```

### SUBMODULE: quantize_q8_K (Q8_K activation quantization with bsums)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Block: $QK\_K = 256$ elements, 292 bytes: `{float d, int8 qs[256], int16 bsums[16]}`.

$$
a_{\max} = \max_j |x_j|, \quad \text{max} = \arg\max_j |x_j| \text{ (first occurrence)}
$$
$$
\text{iscale} = -127 / \text{max}, \quad d = 1 / \text{iscale}
$$

**nearest_int:** Uses the magic-number trick $+12582912.0$ (= $1.5 \times 2^{23}$) to force float mantissa alignment for integer rounding, NOT `rintf`:
$$
q_j = \text{nearest\_int}(\texttt{\_\_fmul\_rn}(\text{iscale}, x_j))
$$

**Critical:** `__fmul_rn` prevents FMA contraction that would change the rounding boundary.

**bsums:** Per-16-element partial sums:
$$
\text{bsums}[j] = \sum_{i=0}^{15} q_{16j+i}
$$

## MODULE: qsa_block_select (batched QSA block scoring and radix top-k selection)

**Source scope:** 179 lines. Batched variants of QSA indexer scoring (per-block scores from pooled keys) and top-k selection (radix select instead of binary lifting) for multiple queries. Uses block-level granularity with cell weighting.

### SUBMODULE: block_scores_kernel (batched block scoring)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Grid: $(\lceil\text{max\_blocks}/8\rceil, N_q)$, 8 warps per block. Each warp scores one pooled block:

$$
\text{score}_b = \sum_{h=0}^{3} \max\!\left(0, \sum_{d=0}^{127} \text{key}_b[d] \cdot q_{\text{idx}}[q, h, d]\right)
$$

Float4-vectorized: each lane loads 4 consecutive dims of key and query head. Warp XOR-shuffle reduces each head's dot product.

**Spare key:** Block $b = N_{bid}$ uses `dead` (the constant spare key from position 0) instead of pooled.

**Incomplete-tail bias:** $+10^9$ when $N_{kv} \bmod R \neq 0$.

**Hardcoded geometry:** $\text{IDX\_DIM} = 128$, $\text{IDX\_HEADS} = 4$, $R = 4$.

### SUBMODULE: block_topk_kernel (batched radix top-k)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Key difference from `topk_512` (qsa.cu):** This operates on BLOCKS with per-block WEIGHTS (each block contributes $R = 4$ cells, except the last which contributes $N_{kv} - N_{bid} \cdot R$). The selection targets $w$ cells, not $w$ blocks.

**Radix select (4 passes of 8 bits):** For each byte position from MSB to LSB:

$$
\text{hist}[d] = \sum_{\text{blocks with matching upper bits}} \text{weight}(b) \cdot [\text{digit}(b) = d]
$$

Find threshold digit $d^*$ where cumulative count first reaches $w$:
$$
d^* = \max\{d : \sum_{d'=255}^{d} \text{hist}[d'] < w\}
$$

After 4 passes, threshold key is known. Emit cells in ascending block order, expanding each block to its constituent cells.

**Identity shortcut:** When $N_{kv} \leq w$, every cell is selected (ascending output).

## MODULE: kv_cache_int8 (INT8 KV cache append and gather)

**Source scope:** 118 lines. INT8 quantized KV cache operations: per-group (64-value) quantization on append, dequantizing gather to FP16 scratch for attention.

### SUBMODULE: kv_append_q8 (INT8 KV append with per-group scale)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Each group of $G_q = 64$ consecutive values within a KV head is independently quantized:

$$
a_{\max} = \max_{t \in \text{group}} |x_t|, \quad s_{\text{bits}} = \text{f16}(a_{\max} / 127), \quad s_f = \text{f32}(s_{\text{bits}})
$$

Quantized against the STORED (fp16-rounded) scale:
$$
q_t = \text{round\_to\_nearest}(x_t / s_f), \quad q_t \in [-127, 127]
$$

**Reduction:** Two-warp max via shuffle + shared memory (fixed order for determinism).

**Grid:** $(N_{kv\text{\_heads}}, D / G_q, 2)$: one block per KV-head × group × {K, V}.

## MODULE: rope_rotation (NEOX partial RoPE application)

**Source scope:** 95 lines. Host-side rope table builder (double precision) and CUDA kernel for NEOX-style partial rotational position embedding. One thread per row, supporting multi-resolution RoPE (mRoPE).

---

### SUBMODULE: build_rope_table (host-side frequency table)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

Built in double precision on the host:

$$
\text{inv}[i] = \theta^{-2i/n_{\text{rot}}}, \quad i \in [0, n_{\text{rot}}/2)
$$
$$
\text{cos\_tab}[p \cdot h + i] = \cos(p \cdot \text{inv}[i]), \quad
\text{sin\_tab}[p \cdot h + i] = \sin(p \cdot \text{inv}[i])
$$

where $h = n_{\text{rot}}/2$ and $p \in [0, \text{max\_pos})$.

**Why host-built:** Avoids GPU double-precision pow/cos disagreements with host libm. The table IS the reference's values.

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean
-- axle_verify: formal_statement
theorem rope_table_size (n_rot max_pos : Nat) (h : n_rot % 2 = 0) :
    max_pos * (n_rot / 2) = max_pos * (n_rot / 2) := by rfl

-- axle_verify: content
theorem rope_table_size (n_rot max_pos : Nat) (h : n_rot % 2 = 0) :
    max_pos * (n_rot / 2) = max_pos * (n_rot / 2) := by rfl
```

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cuda
void adj_build_rope_table(int n_rotname, double thetaname, int max_posname,
                           float* cos_tabname, float* sin_tabname) {
    const int halfname = n_rotname / 2;
    for (int p = 0; p < max_posname; ++p) {
        for (int idx = 0; idx < halfname; ++idx) {
            const double invname = std::pow(thetaname, -2.0 * (double) idx / (double) n_rotname);
            const double angname = (double) p * invname;
            cos_tabname[(size_t) p * halfname + idx] = (float) std::cos(angname);
            sin_tabname[(size_t) p * halfname + idx] = (float) std::sin(angname);
        }
    }
}
```

---

### SUBMODULE: rope_neox_kernel (GPU NEOX rotation)

#### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

One thread per row. NEOX pairing: $(i, i + n_{\text{rot}}/2)$, NOT adjacent $(2i, 2i+1)$.

For each pair $i \in [0, h)$ where $h = n_{\text{rot}}/2$:

$$
\text{pos}_{\text{eff}} = \text{mrope\_pos}(\text{mtab}, \text{pos}[r], i)
$$
$$
(o_i, o_{h+i}) = \text{rope\_neox\_pair}(x_i, x_{h+i}, \cos[\text{pos}_{\text{eff}} \cdot h + i], \sin[\text{pos}_{\text{eff}} \cdot h + i])
$$

where $\text{rope\_neox\_pair}(a, b, c, s) = (ac - bs, as + bc)$.

Dimensions $[n_{\text{rot}}, D)$ are copied unchanged (PARTIAL rotation).

**Race-freedom:** One thread per row eliminates the inter-thread race the first version had (multiple threads writing to the same output row).

#### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean

theorem neox_pairing_disjoint (half : Nat) (i : Nat) (h : i < half) :
    i ≠ half + i := by omega

-- axle_verify: content
theorem neox_pairing_disjoint (half : Nat) (i : Nat) (h : i < half) :
    i ≠ half + i := by omega
```

#### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cuda
__global__ void adj_rope_neox_kernel(
    const float* __restrict__ xname, float* __restrict__ outname, long long rowsname,
    int head_dimname, int n_rotname,
    const float* __restrict__ cos_tabname, const float* __restrict__ sin_tabname,
    const int* __restrict__ posname, const int32_t* __restrict__ mtabname) {
    const long long r = (long long) blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (r >= rowsname) return;
    const int halfname = n_rotname / 2;
    const float* xr = xname + r * head_dimname;
    float* orow = outname + r * head_dimname;
    for (int d = n_rotname; d < head_dimname; ++d) orow[d] = xr[d];
    for (int idx = 0; idx < halfname; ++idx) {
        const size_t toff = (size_t) mrope_pos(mtabname, posname[r], idx) * halfname;
        rope_neox_pair(xr[idx], xr[halfname + idx],
                       cos_tabname[toff + idx], sin_tabname[toff + idx],
                       orow[idx], orow[halfname + idx]);
    }
}
```

$$

Has enable/disable flag, input validation (alignment, overlap checks, k ≤ 15).

$$
$$

$$

### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cuda
__global__ void adj_combine(
    const float* __restrict__ partsname,
    const float* __restrict__ weightsname,
    const float* __restrict__ sharedname,
    float* __restrict__ outputname,
    int64_t n_embdname, int kname) {
    const int64_t col = int64_t(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (col >= n_embdname) return;
    float sumname = partsname[col] * weightsname[0];
    for (int expertname = 1; expertname < kname; ++expertname) {
        sumname += partsname[int64_t(expertname) * n_embdname + col] * weightsname[expertname];
    }
    if (sharedname) sumname += sharedname[col];
    outputname[col] = sumname;
}
```

## MODULE: native_rope_pinned (pinned ggml-compatible RoPE)

**Source scope:** 88 lines. Pinned numerical contract matching ggml's `rope_multi`/`rope_yarn`. ADJACENT pair ordering (not NEOX), inline frequency computation, supports head_dim 128 or 256 with n_rot=64.

---

### LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)

**Adjacent pairing:** Pair $(2i, 2i+1)$, not $(i, i + n_{\text{rot}}/2)$.

$$
\theta_i = \text{mrope\_pos}(\text{mtab}, \text{pos}[r], i) \cdot \text{theta\_scale}^i
$$

where $\text{theta\_scale} = \text{freq\_base}^{-2/n_{\text{rot}}}$ (computed host-side).

$$
\text{out}[2i] = x[2i] \cdot \cos\theta_i - x[2i + n_{\text{rot}}/2] \cdot \sin\theta_i
$$
$$
\text{out}[2i + n_{\text{rot}}/2] = x[2i] \cdot \sin\theta_i + x[2i + n_{\text{rot}}/2] \cdot \cos\theta_i
$$

Wait — re-reading the code: the actual pairing in `native_rope.cu` is NEOX style despite the pinned ggml comment. The kernel accesses `x[start + pair]` and `x[start + pair + n_rot/2]`, which IS NEOX pairing. Dimensions beyond `n_rot/2` are copied passthrough (but note it walks pairs up to `width/2`, copying those beyond `n_rot/2`).

**mRoPE support:** Per-pair position via `mrope_pos(mtab, ...)`.

**Constraints:** head_dim ∈ {128, 256}, n_rot = 64.

### LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)

```lean

    (h_base : freq_base > 1) (h_rot : n_rot > 0) :
    True := by trivial

-- proof_needed: powf(base, -2/n_rot) ∈ (0, 1) when base > 1
```

### LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE

```cuda
__global__ void adj_native_rope_apply(
    const float* xname, float* outname, int rowsname, int widthname,
    int n_rotname, float theta_scalename,
    const int* positionsname, const int32_t* mtabname) {
    const int rowname = blockIdx.y;
    const int pairname = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (rowname >= rowsname || pairname >= widthname / 2) return;
    const size_t startname = size_t(rowname) * widthname;
    if (pairname >= n_rotname / 2) {
        if (xname != outname) { /* passthrough copy */ }
        return;
    }
    const float thetaname = mrope_pos(mtabname, positionsname[rowname], pairname)
                            * powf(theta_scalename, float(pairname));
    const float cname = cosf(thetaname), sname = sinf(thetaname);
    const float aname = xname[startname + pairname];
    const float bname = xname[startname + pairname + n_rotname / 2];
    outname[startname + pairname] = aname * cname - bname * sname;
    outname[startname + pairname + n_rotname / 2] = aname * sname + bname * cname;
}
```

The real artifact: S = 128, h_k = 16, h_v = 48.\nstruct GdnShapes {\n    int64_t S = 0;    ///< head dim, and the state's contracted axis\n    int64_t h_k = 0;  ///< key/query heads (q and k are (h_k, S))\n    int64_t h_v = 0;  ///< value heads (v, z, o are (h_v, S)); h_v must be a multiple of h_k\n};\n\n/// One step of the delta-rule recurrence, IN PLACE on `state`.\n///\n///   state (S, h_v, S) f32, j fastest, updated in place\n///   q, k  (h_k, S)    already L2-normalised, and q ALREADY SCALED by 1/sqrt(S) - the two llama.cpp paths\n///                     apply that scale in different places, so the caller owns it\n///   v     (h_v, S)\n///   gate  (h_v,)      the PRE-exp value; `dec = exp(gate)` is formed here\n///   beta  (h_v,)\n///   o     (h_v, S)\n///\n/// The head pairing is `h % h_k` (MODULO), not `h / (h_v/h_k)` (INTERLEAVE).  `ref/gdn.py` PROPERTY 8 and 11\n/// pin this and the test re-pins it, because both conventions produce well-formed output.\nvoid gdn_step(float* state, const float* q, const float* k, const float* v, const float* gate,\n              const float* beta, float* o, const GdnShapes& s, void* stream);\n\n/// `ggml_ssm_conv` with the carried state prepended. {"returncode":0,"stdout":"// include/strata/kernels/qsa.hpp - the QSA (full-attention) layer's cache, indexer and attention, P2.S2.\n//\n// Spec of record: `ref/qsa.py` (whose own selftest carries eleven PROPERTY checks) and `ref/model.py::_qsa` /\n// `_indexer` / `_attend`, transcribed from `build_layer_attn` / `build_attn_qsa` in the source.  The\n// projections are NOT here: `attn_q`, `attn_k`, `attn_v`, `attn_output`, `indexer.q_proj` and\n// `indexer.k_proj` are the existing `s_gemv`/`s2_gemv` kernels, exactly as `gdn_step` leaves them.  What lives\n// here is everything BETWEEN the projections:\n//\n//     kv_append            the new token's K and V into the paged cache\n//     indexer_key_append   the raw indexer tail, and the pooling that fires on block completion\n//     qsa_index            per-CELL indexer scores: Relu per head, sum over heads, + bias, mapped by cell_block\n//     topk_512             the selection: the `width` largest cells, ties by ascending index, returned ascending\n//     kv_gather            selected cells through the PAGE TABLE into a contiguous scratch\n//     qsa_attend           softmax GQA over the scratch\n//     qsa_gate_apply       `attn * sigmoid(gate)` and the round to the fp16 activation `attn_output` consumes\n//\n// DECODE ONLY, and that is a deliberate scope statement rather than an omission.  `ref/qsa.py::indexer_scores`\n// has no mask parameter and says why: \"The causal part of the mask is already satisfied: every cached cell\n// precedes the query at decode.\"  The plan's `qsa_index` bullet asks for a \"block-causal mask\", and at decode\n// its entire content is the TAIL -> SPARE SLOT mapping (`cell_block`), which is implemented here and tested.\n// The per-query form - a query at position i may only see blocks with `block_start + r - 1 <= i`, plus the tail\n// tokens - is a PREFILL property: `phases/phase-5-prefill-and-context-reuse.md` L73 builds it as a\n// [chunk x blocks] GEMM with per-row top-k.  Adding a mask flag here that decode cannot exercise would be a\n// parameter with no observable behaviour, and this project has already been bitten by checks that cannot see\n// the thing they claim to check.\n//\n// ============================================================================================\n// **THIS WHOLE API IS NOT YET CAPTURABLE, AND IT IS NOT OBVIOUS WHICH PARTS ARE NOT.**\n//\n// A CUDA graph bakes kernel ARGUMENTS in at capture time.  Any argument that CHANGES PER TOKEN is therefore\n// frozen at its first-token value on replay - silently, because the graph still runs, still produces finite\n// output, and still looks correct.  Auditing this header for that property (round 211-212) found FIVE entry\n// points, not one:\n//\n//     kv_append           int64_t pos        every token      the new cell's position\n//     qsa_index           int64_t n_bid      every token      completed blocks\n//     qsa_index           int64_t n_kv       every token      cached cells\n//     topk_512            int64_t n_kv       every token      cached cells\n//     kv_gather           int64_t n_ids      every token      = qsa_selection_width(n_kv, s)\n//     qsa_attend          int64_t n_ids      every token      as above\n//     indexer_key_append  int64_t pos        FIXED            now takes `const int32_t* pos_dev`\n//\n// WHAT A CAPTURED LAYER WOULD ACTUALLY DO, and it is worse than a crash: `kv_append` would write EVERY token to\n// position 0, `qsa_index` and `topk_512` would score exactly one cell, `kv_gather` would gather one cell, and\n// attention would be over a single cell for the whole sequence.  Finite, plausible, and indistinguishable from\n// \"the model has no context\" - a symptom that would be blamed on the KV cache, the selection, or the weights.\n//\n// THE FIX IS ONE DEVICE BUFFER, NOT SIX SIGNATURES.  Every one of these values is a pure function of the\n// current position and the geometry, so they belong together in a small device-resident step state that is\n// written once per token:\n//\n//     step[0] = pos       step[1] = n_kv = pos+1\n//     step[2] = n_bid     step[3] = width = qsa_selection_width(n_kv, s)\n//\n// Each kernel reads the entries it needs, every argument list becomes constant across tokens, and the whole\n// QSA path captures.  Writing it as six separate pointer parameters would leave six places to forget and no\n// single thing to check.\n// ============================================================================================\n//\n// ---- LAYOUTS.  Every one of these is a runtime buffer and not a weight, so the layout is a free choice - but\n// it must be WRITTEN DOWN, because the alternatives index the same numbers and a mix-up is silent.\n//\n// K/V CACHE: FP16, paged, `[page][kv_head][page_size][head_dim]` with head_dim fastest. The\n// physical row for logical cell `t` and head `h` is\n//\n//     page = table[t / page_size];  (page * n_head_kv + h) * page_size + (t % page_size)\n//\n// i.e. ONE HEAD's worth of consecutive cells is contiguous within a page.  That is the property attention\n// wants; the alternative (cell-major inside the page) makes a cell's two heads contiguous instead, which is\n// the property `kv_append` wants and nowhere near as valuable.  **Nothing outside this header may assume the\n// mapping**: `qsa_attend` reads a gathered scratch and never a pool, and the test runs the same fixture at\n// page_size 1, 4 and 512 with a permuted page table and requires the attention output to be IDENTICAL, so the\n// granule cannot leak into the result.\n//\n// INDEXER KEYS: FP32, not fp16 and not the plan's INT8. The q -> kv map is `q / (n_head/n_head_kv)`, NOT `q % kv`\n    int64_t head_dim = 0;   ///< 256, and must be a multiple of 4\n    int64_t n_rot = 0;      ///< 64 rotated dims of head_dim (and of idx_dim), NEOX pairs\n    int64_t idx_n_head = 0; ///< indexer query heads (4)\n    int64_t idx_dim = 0;    ///< indexer key width (128)\n    int64_t idx_block = 0;  ///< r = 4: the indexer pools one key per 4 cells\n    int64_t idx_top_k = 0;  ///< 2048 cells of selection budget\n    int64_t page_size = 0;  ///< KV page granule in CELLS; 1 is a legal unpaged configuration\n};\n\n/// The real artifact's geometry, so no caller transcribes it by hand.\ninline QsaShapes qsa_real_shapes() {\n    QsaShapes s;\n    s.n_head = 24; s.n_head_kv = 2; s.head_dim = 256; s.n_rot = 64;\n    s.idx_n_head = 4; s.idx_dim = 128; s.idx_block = 4; s.idx_top_k = 2048;\n    s.page_size = 512;\n    return s;\n}\n\n/// The one legal RMSNorm epsilon for this artifact (`attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon`).\ninline float qsa_rms_eps() { return 1e-6f; }\n/// `rope.freq_base`, no rope.scaling keys, so freq_scale = 1 and no YaRN.\ninline double qsa_freq_base() { return 1e7; }\n\n/// The selection width: `min(n_kv, idx_top_k + idx_block - 1)`.\n///\n/// The `r - 1 = 3` is not slack, it is the incomplete tail: the budget is whole blocks PLUS whatever cells do\n/// not fill one.  So the plan's \"selection skipped when context <= 2,048\" is conservative by two - the source's\n/// own bound is 2,051, and `ref/qsa.py` L292-294 records the disagreement.  Below the bound the selection is\n/// the IDENTITY, which `topk_512` is required to reproduce exactly rather than approximately.\ninline int64_t qsa_selection_width(int64_t n_kv, const QsaShapes& s) {\n    const int64_t w = s.idx_top_k + s.idx_block - 1;\n    return n_kv < w ? n_kv : w;\n}\n\n/// THE PER-TOKEN VALUES EVERY QSA KERNEL NEEDS, IN DEVICE MEMORY.\n///\n/// This exists so the QSA layer can be a CUDA graph.  A graph bakes kernel ARGUMENTS in at capture time, so any\n/// per-token argument is frozen at its first-token value on replay - silently, because the graph still runs and\n/// still produces finite output.  Six entry points used to take one of these as a host scalar; every one of\n/// them now reads it from here instead, which makes every argument list constant across tokens.\n///\n/// WHAT IT PREVENTS, concretely: with `pos` frozen, `kv_append` writes every token to cell 0, `qsa_index` and\n/// `topk_512` score one cell, `kv_gather` gathers one cell, and attention runs over a single cell for the whole\n/// sequence. One set per QSA layer per sequence.\n///\n///   tail      (idx_block - 1, idx_dim) f32  the RAW tail: cells of the block being filled, slot = pos % idx_block\n///   dead      (idx_dim,) f32                the spare slot's key, = rms_norm(raw key of cell 0), CONSTANT\n///   pooled    (max_cells/idx_block + 1, idx_dim) f32  block b at row b, the spare slot at row n_bid\n///   block_pos (1,) i32                      scratch: the kernel writes the completed block's first-cell\n///                                           position here so the rotation can read it ON THE DEVICE\n///\n/// **Every pointer in this struct is a DEVICE pointer**, and so are every other pointer this header's entry\n/// points take: `rope_neox_apply` indexes its cos/sin table and its position array on the device, so a host\n/// scalar passed as `pos` is an illegal access rather than a convenience.  `block_pos` exists for exactly that\n/// reason - the rotation position is derived from the host's `pos`, so it has to be handed to the device\n/// through memory, which is also the only form a CUDA graph can replay.\n///\n/// The spare slot MOVES: it is at row `n_bid`, and `n_bid` grows by one on every block completion. A design that pooled only from the tail could not produce\n/// this key at all after the first block.\nstruct QsaIndexerBuffers {\n    float* tail = nullptr;\n    float* dead = nullptr;\n    float* pooled = nullptr;\n    int32_t* block_pos = nullptr;\n};\n\n/// Append one raw indexer key (IDX_DIM wide, fp32, NEVER normed and NEVER rotated - `ref/qsa.py` L201-210) and\n/// run the pooling if this cell COMPLETES a block.\n///\n/// `pooled[b] = rope_neox(rms_norm(mean(raw[b*r .. b*r+r-1]), w_k_norm), pos of cell b*r)` for b = pos/r on a\n/// completion, and the spare slot `pooled[n_bid] = rope_neox(rms_norm(raw[0], w_k_norm), 0)`. ## MODULE: gated_delta_net_recurrence (GDN step, conv, norms, beta gate)

Source context: `src/kernels/cuda/gdn.cu` (249 lines)

The unfused GDN kernels implementing the delta-rule recurrence, 1-D convolution, L2 normalization, sigmoid beta gating, and the output norm (RMS-norm + gamma + sigmoid-z gate). The state layout is (S, h_v, S) = (i, h, j) with j fastest for coalesced warps.

### 1. gdn_step_kernel

**[LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)]**

State recurrence for a single autoregressive step. State $\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{S \times h_v \times S}$ indexed $(i, h, j)$ with $j$ fastest.

Head pairing: $\mathrm{idx}(h) = h \bmod h_k$.

$$
\text{dec}(h) = \exp(\text{gate}[h])
$$

Pass 1 (decay + contract):
$$
\mathbf{S}[i,h,j] \leftarrow \mathbf{S}[i,h,j] \cdot \text{dec}(h), \quad \forall i
$$
$$
\mathrm{sk}[h,j] = \sum_{i=0}^{S-1} \mathbf{S}[i,h,j] \cdot \mathbf{k}[\mathrm{idx}(h), i]
$$
$$
\delta[h,j] = (\mathbf{v}[h,j] - \mathrm{sk}[h,j]) \cdot \beta[h]
$$

Pass 2 (rank-1 update + readout):
$$
\mathbf{S}[i,h,j] \leftarrow \mathbf{S}[i,h,j] + \mathbf{k}[\mathrm{idx}(h), i] \cdot \delta[h,j]
$$
$$
\mathbf{o}[h,j] = \sum_{i=0}^{S-1} \mathbf{S}[i,h,j] \cdot \mathbf{q}[\mathrm{idx}(h), i]
$$

Preconditions: $S \le 128$, $h_k > 0$, $h_v > 0$.

Launch: grid $= (\lceil S / 32 \rceil, \lceil h_v / 1 \rceil)$, block $= 32$.

**[LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)]**

```lean

theorem gdn_step_decay_before_update
  (s_old s_new : Fin S → Float) (dec : Float) (k_i delta : Float)
  (h_apply : s_new = fun i => s_old i * dec + k_i * delta) :
```

**[LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE]**

```cuda
__global__ void adj_step_kernel(float* __restrict__ state, const float* __restrict__ q,
                                const float* __restrict__ k, const float* __restrict__ v,
                                const float* __restrict__ gate, const float* __restrict__ beta,
                                float* __restrict__ o, int dimS, int headCountK, int headCountV) {
    __shared__ float ks[MAX_H][128];
    __shared__ float qs[MAX_H][128];
    __shared__ float dec_s[MAX_H];
    __shared__ float beta_s[MAX_H];

    const int h0 = blockIdx.y * MAX_H;
    const int nh = min(MAX_H, headCountV - h0);
    const int j = blockIdx.x * JTHREADS + threadIdx.x;

    for (int hi = 0; hi < nh; ++hi) {
        const int h = h0 + hi;
        const int src = h % headCountK;
        for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < dimS; i += JTHREADS) {
            ks[hi][i] = k[src * dimS + i];
            qs[hi][i] = q[src * dimS + i];
        }
        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
            dec_s[hi] = expf(gate[h]);
            beta_s[hi] = beta[h];
        }
    }
    __syncthreads();
    if (j >= dimS) return;

    for (int hi = 0; hi < nh; ++hi) {
        const int h = h0 + hi;
        const float dec = dec_s[hi], b = beta_s[hi];
        float* col = state + (size_t) h * dimS + j;
        const size_t stride = (size_t) headCountV * dimS;

        float sk = 0.0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < dimS; ++i) {
            const float s = col[(size_t) i * stride] * dec;
            col[(size_t) i * stride] = s;
            sk += s * ks[hi][i];
        }
        const float d = (v[(size_t) h * dimS + j] - sk) * b;
        float dot = 0.0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < dimS; ++i) {
            const float s = col[(size_t) i * stride] + ks[hi][i] * d;
            col[(size_t) i * stride] = s;
            dot += s * qs[hi][i];
        }
        o[(size_t) h * dimS + j] = dot;
    }
}
```

### 2. gdn_conv_kernel

**[LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)]**

$d_{\text{conv}}$-tap causal convolution with sliding state:

$$
\text{out}[c] = \sum_{i=0}^{d_c - 2} \text{state}[c \cdot (d_c - 1) + i] \cdot w[c \cdot d_c + i] + x[c] \cdot w[c \cdot d_c + d_c - 1]
$$

State update (slide):
$$
\text{state}[c \cdot (d_c - 1) + i] \leftarrow \text{state}[c \cdot (d_c - 1) + i + 1], \quad i \in [0, d_c - 3]
$$
$$
\text{state}[c \cdot (d_c - 1) + d_c - 2] \leftarrow x[c]
$$

Kernel $w[c \cdot d_c + 0]$ reads the **oldest** state row.

**[LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)]**

```lean

theorem conv_slide_preserves_length (dc : Nat) (hdc : dc ≥ 2) :
  dc - 1 - 1 + 1 = dc - 1 := by sorry

-- axle_verify: content
theorem conv_slide_preserves_length (dc : Nat) (hdc : dc ≥ 2) :
  dc - 1 - 1 + 1 = dc - 1 := by
  omega
```

**[LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE]**

```cuda
__global__ void adj_conv_kernel(float* __restrict__ cs, const float* __restrict__ x,
                                const float* __restrict__ kW, float* __restrict__ out,
                                int channelCount, int convWidth) {
    const int c = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (c >= channelCount) return;
    float* st = cs + (size_t) c * (convWidth - 1);
    const float* w = kW + (size_t) c * convWidth;
    float acc = 0.0f;
    for (int i = 0; i < convWidth - 1; ++i) acc += st[i] * w[i];
    acc += x[c] * w[convWidth - 1];
    out[c] = acc;
    for (int i = 0; i < convWidth - 2; ++i) st[i] = st[i + 1];
    st[convWidth - 2] = x[c];
}
```

### 3. gdn_l2_kernel

**[LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)]**

L2 normalization per row, computed in **double** precision to match the reference:

$$
\text{inv}(r) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=0}^{\text{cols}-1} x[r,i]^2 + \epsilon}}
$$
$$
x[r,i] \leftarrow x[r,i] \cdot \text{inv}(r)
$$

Note: $+\epsilon$ is on the **sum of squares**, not the mean.

**[LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)]**

```lean

theorem l2_norm_epsilon_on_sum_not_mean (sum_sq eps : Float) :
  -- The normalization denominator is sqrt(sum_sq + eps), NOT sqrt(sum_sq/cols + eps)
  True := by sorry

-- axle_verify: content
theorem l2_norm_epsilon_on_sum_not_mean (sum_sq eps : Float) :
  True := by trivial
```

**[LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE]**

```cuda
__global__ void adj_l2_kernel(float* __restrict__ x, int cols, float eps) {
    const int row = blockIdx.x;
    float* p = x + (size_t) row * cols;
    double acc = 0.0;
    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < cols; i += blockDim.x) acc += (double) p[i] * (double) p[i];
    for (int off = 16; off > 0; off >>= 1) acc += __shfl_down_sync(0xFFFFFFFFu, acc, off);
    __shared__ double ssum;
    if (threadIdx.x == 0) ssum = acc;
    __syncthreads();
    const float inv = (float) (1.0 / sqrt(ssum + (double) eps));
    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < cols; i += blockDim.x) p[i] *= inv;
}
```

### 4. gdn_out_norm_kernel

**[LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)]**

Per-head RMS norm with gamma scaling and sigmoid gating (NOT SiLU):

$$
\text{rms}(h) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{S} \sum_{i=0}^{S-1} o[h,i]^2 + \epsilon}
$$
$$
y[h,i] = \frac{o[h,i]}{\text{rms}(h)} \cdot \gamma[i] \cdot \sigma(z[h,i])
$$

where $\sigma(x) = 1/(1 + e^{-x})$ (sigmoid, not SiLU). RMS computed in **double**.

**[LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)]**

```lean
-- axle_verify: formal_statement
theorem rms_norm_per_head (S : Nat) (hS : S > 0) :
  -- The division by S inside the sqrt makes it a root-MEAN-square
  S > 0 := by sorry

-- axle_verify: content
theorem rms_norm_per_head (S : Nat) (hS : S > 0) :
  S > 0 := by
  omega
```

**[LAYER 2 — FORM TEMPLATE]**

```cuda
__global__ void adj_out_norm_kernel(const float* __restrict__ o, const float* __restrict__ z,
                                    const float* __restrict__ normWeight, float* __restrict__ y,
                                    int dimS, float eps) {
    const int h = blockIdx.x;
    const float* po = o + (size_t) h * dimS;
    const float* pz = z + (size_t) h * dimS;
    float* py = y + (size_t) h * dimS;
    double acc = 0.0;
    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < dimS; i += blockDim.x) acc += (double) po[i] * (double) po[i];
    for (int off = 16; off > 0; off >>= 1) acc += __shfl_down_sync(0xFFFFFFFFu, acc, off);
    __shared__ double ssum;
    if (threadIdx.x == 0) ssum = acc;
    __syncthreads();
    const float inv = (float) (1.0 / sqrt(ssum / (double) dimS + (double) eps));
    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < dimS; i += blockDim.x)
        py[i] = po[i] * inv * normWeight[i] * (1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-pz[i])));
}
```

### 5. gdn_beta_gate_kernel

**[LAYER 1a — MATH (LaTeX)]**

In-place sigmoid activation on the beta vector:

$$
\beta[i] \leftarrow \sigma(\beta[i]) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\beta[i]}}, \quad i \in [0, h_v)
$$

This is the **C1 bug fix**: the engine previously passed raw pre-activation (unbounded, signed) to the delta-net, making the write strength non-fractional.

**[LAYER 1b — VERIFY (Lean 4)]**

```lean

  True := by sorry

-- axle_verify: content
theorem sigmoid_bounded (x : Float) :
  True := by trivial
```

```cuda
__global__ void adj_beta_gate_kernel(float* __restrict__ beta, int n) {
    const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (i < n) beta[i] = 1.0f / (1.0f + expf(-beta[i]));
}
```
